course_title: Common and Specific Factors in Mental Health Treatments

learning_outcomes.description: Recognise key concepts and critically review the common and specific factors paradigm in mental health treatments
Identify and differentiate how relevant Art Therapy and Psychotherapy traditions conceive the different phases of treatment and common factors in mental health treatment
Practice basic therapeutic skills relative to common factors approach and to relevant Art Therapy and Psychotherapy traditions

assessments.assessment_title: Quiz / reflection on practicing a common factor during Workshops
assessments.task_description:
During the workshops, you will be required to hand write a reflection on your experience practicing a common factor. The lecturer will give you more details of the question you will address on the day. You will write your reflection and hand your answer sheet to the lecturer when you finish, which should not take more than 15 minutes. Students are expected to use the content learned during the workshops for the reflection, and will not have access to book, computers or other devices to complete the reflection.

Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against a rubric that will be available for students.

Each weekly post is due before the start of the tutorial for that week.
assessments.task_description:
Before each tutorial, you will post a 300-word response (±10%) to the week's questions on the discussion board. Your responses must a) refer to concepts from the assigned readings and, b) include a reflection on something you learned from practicing this common factor. Questions and readings will be available in the 'learning activities' tab of the Course Profile. You will submit your post through the "Discussion Board" tab on the Learn.UQ course site. No bibliographical references are needed.

Even though AI use is permitted, the focus of this assessment is your capacity to analyse knowledge, reflect and demonstrate your own thinking. Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against the below rubric.

Marking Rubric:

Maximum points: 25 (10 posts with maximum points per post)

Maximum points per post: 2.5 if posted on time (0 points = if not posted)

Breakdown of criteria contribution to the 2.5 points per post:

1.    Responds questions using relevant concepts from readings = 1 point. No concepts from the readings = 0 points

2.    Includes student’s reflection on learning from experience applying factor = 1 point. Only citing article, no original ideas from the student = 0 points

3.    Well written & within 300-word limit (10% tolerance) = 0.5 points. Under or over word limit, poor writing quality = 0 points

assessments.assessment_title: Lead tutorial discussion about a common factor
assessments.category: Participation/ Student contribution, Presentation, Tutorial/ Problem Set
assessments.task_description:
In this activity you will present to the tutorial group a critical analysis of the arguments in favour and against recognising a given therapeutic task as a common factor across different therapeutic traditions. In this discussion, you will first present the arguments and evidence in favour of this claim, including evidence of its presence in two different therapeutic interventions. Then you will play the "Devil’s advocate" role and consider arguments against recognising this aspect of therapy as a ‘common factor’. Be mindful that that you might be asked to discuss a common factor that enjoys wide recognition, one that is emerging or is contentious: in these last cases you might need to infer or ‘read between lines’ to identify this factor within the therapeutic traditions you analyse. Your presentation should be clear, articulate and appealing, following post-graduate standards, citing or identifying authors or sources as necessary, to differentiate them from your own ideas. If you wish, you can use PowerPoint slides and other resources to support your presentation. The presentation will take up to 15 minutes. At the end of the presentation your tutor will lead a brief Q&A session with you to then pass to the open discussion with the tutorial group.

At the start of the semester the tutor will decide with students the roster of presentations for the rest of the semester. Students should send the 'bare bones' of their presentation to the tutors or course coordinator one week before the presentation date to be checked, get feedback and support as needed. Approved materials for this assessment are the required readings. Any other reading needs to be approved by your tutor or course coordinator. The use of AI is allowed prior discussion with the tutor or course coordinator for purposes such as enhancing clarity of text, and surveying the existence of other valuable content, in which case it should be acknowledged during the presentation.

Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against a rubric available to students, and it will be recorded for eventual review purposes.

Summarising, during your presentation you should:

a) Identify and define the common factor you want to discuss. Brief history (if it’s already recognised as such), it's clinical relevance and supporting research.

b) Present the arguments in favour of this common factor, analysing how it manifests it two distinctive traditions.

c) Present the arguments against considering this therapeutic task as a common factor.

d) Present a clear, well organised, articulate and visually appealing presentation (you might use PowerPoint slides), respecting the 10-15 minutes for the presentation and the following 10-minute Q&A session. The exact duration of the presentation will be determined and communicated by the tutor (based on the number of students presenting on the same day).

assessments.assessment_title: Application of a common factor into your clinical practice
assessments.task_description:
As we have seen through the semester, common factors are conceptualised and practiced differently across various therapeutic traditions. For this assessment, you will present a clinical vignette from your own clinical practice in which you apply one of the common factors discussed in this course, including the impact this intervention had over the client. You will then discuss how the particular way in which you practice this common factor might reflect a particular therapeutic tradition you practice and identify with, and then reflect on the benefits and disadvantages of the way you conceive and practiced this common factor compared to how its conceived and practice by an alternative tradition.

Even though AI use is permitted, the focus of this assessment is your capacity to analyse knowledge, reflect and demonstrate independent thinking. The use Artificial Intelligence (AI) for the essay should be appropriately acknowledged in the references.

Following UQ guidelines, this assessment will marked against a rubric that will be available for students.

In summary:

1. Provide a clinical vignette of a case demonstrating the use of a common factor, including the effect this intervention had over the client, explaining how you came to this conclusion.

2. Identify the therapeutic tradition that informs the way you practice this common factor, explaining how you came to this conclusion, and explaining how this relates with your previous training and/or identity as therapist..

3. Reflect on the benefits and disadvantages of the way you practice this common factor compared to how its conceived and practice by an alternative tradition.

4. Essay is written at a postgraduate level; referencing and citation follow standard format and the word count adheres to limit (excluding references) with +/- 10% tolerance.

T11: Changing maladaptive patterns

Acknowledging our contribution to vicious cycles or karma. Discussion of readings that explore the importance of awareness and self-control to change pathological patterns (behavioural, intrapsychic and interpersonal).

  • How important is insight to change self-defeating habits?
  • What's the role of being accountable for, owning and mastering our behaviour to change toxic habits?
  • Is insight indispensable for change?

Please refer to ‘Learning Resources \\ Course Reading List’ for this session’s compulsory readings.

Art therapy only:

  • Eren,N et al (2014) Psychosocial, symptomatic and diagnostic changes with long-term psychodynamic art psychotherapy for personality disorders, The Arts in Psychotherapy 41 :375 385
